import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Cleaning and Feature Engineering ---
# Drop rows with missing income, as it's crucial for this visualization
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Income']).copy()

# Create 'Total_Spending' column by summing all 'Mnt' (monetary) columns
mnt_cols = [col for col in df_clean.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df_clean['Total_Spending'] = df_clean[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Create 'Num_Dependents' column for family size
df_clean['Num_Dependents'] = df_clean['Kidhome'] + df_clean['Teenhome']

# Simplify 'Marital_Status' into a more digestible category for the legend
df_clean['Relationship_Status'] = df_clean['Marital_Status'].replace({
    'Married': 'In Relationship',
    'Together': 'In Relationship',
    'Single': 'Single',
    'Divorced': 'Single',
    'Widow': 'Single',
    'Alone': 'Single',
    'Absurd': 'Single',
    'YOLO': 'Single'
})

# Filter out extreme outliers for a clearer visualization
income_cap = df_clean['Income'].quantile(0.99)
spending_cap = df_clean['Total_Spending'].quantile(0.99)
df_viz = df_clean[(df_clean['Income'] < income_cap) & (df_clean['Total_Spending'] < spending_cap)]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="muted")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatterplot (bubble chart)
# This chart shows the relationship between Income and Spending,
# with bubble size representing the number of dependents and color representing marital status.
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_viz,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    size='Num_Dependents',
    hue='Relationship_Status',
    sizes=(30, 500),  # Control the range of bubble sizes
    alpha=0.7,
    ax=ax,
    palette={'In Relationship': '#1f77b4', 'Single': '#ff7f0e'} # Use distinct colors
)

# --- Customization and Labels ---
# Main title and subtitle for context
fig.suptitle('Income Drives Spending, Family Size Plays a Key Role', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
ax.set_title('Customer income vs. total spending, segmented by marital status and number of dependents', fontsize=14, pad=20)

# Clear axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending on Products (Last 2 Years)', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)

# Format axis tick labels for readability (e.g., adding commas for thousands)
ax.get_xaxis().set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format(int(x), ',')))
ax.get_yaxis().set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format(int(x), ',')))
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Customize the legend to be clear and well-placed
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually separate handles and labels for the two legends (hue and size)
hue_handles = handles[1:3]
hue_labels = labels[1:3]
size_handles = handles[4:]
size_labels = labels[4:]

# Create a new legend for Marital Status
legend1 = ax.legend(
    hue_handles,
    hue_labels,
    title='Marital Status',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=12
)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Re-add the first legend to the plot

# Create a second legend for the number of Dependents
legend2 = plt.legend(
    size_handles,
    size_labels,
    title='Dependents',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.7),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=12,
    labelspacing=1.5
)

# Improve grid and remove spines for a cleaner look
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and make space for the external legends
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
